title: Linkability between homeowner identity and smart home devices
description: During account registration and device enrollment, the homeowner's personal identity becomes linked to their cameras and sensors, creating a persistent association that could be exploited for profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Registration includes personal identifiers (name, email, address) that are associated with device IDs

title: Identifiability through registration data
description: The homeowner provides personally identifiable information during account registration that directly identifies them as the system user.
assumptions: Registration requires personal identifiers such as name, email, or address

title: Unauthorized disclosure of registration data in transit
description: Account registration and device enrollment data transmitted between homeowner and Home Hub could be intercepted by network attackers, exposing personal information and device configurations.
assumptions: Data transmission occurs over network without guaranteed encryption or could be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks

title: Data integrity compromise during transmission
description: Registration data could be modified in transit, potentially altering device configurations or account credentials before reaching the Home Hub.
assumptions: Network transmission is vulnerable to tampering without integrity verification

title: Persistent linkability at Home Hub storage
description: The Home Hub stores the association between homeowner identity and enrolled devices, creating a centralized link that could be accessed by unauthorized parties or misused.
assumptions: Home Hub maintains persistent storage of registration data linking users to devices

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of what data the Home Hub collects, stores, or processes during registration and device enrollment, including potential secondary uses.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate all data processing activities

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: The Home Hub's processing of homeowner registration data may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding consent, data minimization, or purpose limitation.
assumptions: Registration process may collect more data than necessary or lack proper consent mechanisms
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific implementation and jurisdiction

title: Access code interception during transmission
description: The temporary access code transmitted from Guest User to Home Hub could be intercepted by an attacker monitoring the communication channel, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the front door.
assumptions: The access code is transmitted over a network or wireless channel that could be vulnerable to eavesdropping

title: Access code storage vulnerability
description: The Home Hub may store the access code or access logs in an insecure manner, potentially exposing guest access information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The Home Hub stores access codes or logs access attempts

title: Guest activity correlation
description: The Home Hub could correlate access code usage with guest identity, creating a link between the guest and their physical presence at the property.
assumptions: The Home Hub maintains records linking access codes to guest identities

title: Guest presence detection through system response
description: The Home Hub's response to access code entry (e.g., door unlock confirmation, LED indicators, sound) could reveal to observers that a guest is present at the property.
assumptions: The Home Hub provides observable feedback when access is granted

title: Guest unaware of data processing
description: The guest may be unaware that their access code entry is being logged, stored, or processed by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: Guests are not informed about data processing practices when using access codes

title: Linkability of sensor events to individuals
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written by the Home Hub can be linked to specific individuals' movements and activities within the home, creating detailed behavioral profiles.
assumptions: Sensor events contain timestamps and location data that can be correlated with individual presence

title: Identifiability from sensor event patterns
description: Patterns in motion and door events can identify specific individuals based on their movement patterns, daily routines, and presence in different rooms.
assumptions: Event data contains sufficient granularity to distinguish between different household members

title: Unawareness of event logging
description: Users may not be aware that their motion, door, and sensor activities are being continuously logged and stored in the local event log.
assumptions: Privacy notices or user interfaces do not clearly communicate the extent of event logging

title: Unauthorized access to event log
description: The local event log storing motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing detailed information about household activities and occupancy patterns.
assumptions: Event log has insufficient access controls or is stored without encryption

title: Tampering with event log data
description: The event log could be modified or deleted, allowing actors to cover their tracks or create false records of household activities.
assumptions: Event log lacks integrity controls such as write-once storage or cryptographic signing

title: Linkability through stored event correlations
description: Stored events in the log can be correlated over time to link activities to specific individuals, even if individual events seem anonymous in isolation.
assumptions: Event log retains sufficient historical data for correlation analysis

title: Metadata links video to user identity
description: Home Hub includes metadata (e.g., device ID, timestamps) that can link uploaded video clips to a specific user or household.
assumptions: Metadata is not stripped before upload

title: Data flow linkability to user
description: Network traffic patterns or flow metadata could be monitored to associate the upload activity with a specific user or location.
assumptions: Traffic analysis is possible without decryption

title: Cloud storage links videos to user accounts
description: Cloud Video Storage associates uploaded clips with user accounts, enabling cross-service profiling or tracking.
assumptions: User accounts are linked to video data

title: Identifiable information in video content
description: Recorded clips may contain faces, license plates, or other personally identifiable information (PII) visible in the footage.
assumptions: No automated PII redaction at source

title: Intercepted data reveals identity
description: Unencrypted or weakly encrypted data in transit could be intercepted to extract identifiable information.
assumptions: Encryption may be bypassed or compromised

title: Stored data enables identification
description: Cloud storage retains video content that can be used to identify individuals through facial recognition or other analysis.
assumptions: Data is stored without anonymization

title: Compromised Home Hub leaks data
description: If the Home Hub is compromised, recorded clips could be exfiltrated before upload.
assumptions: Device security is not robust

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Video clips in transit could be intercepted by attackers if encryption is insufficient or misconfigured.
assumptions: Encryption may have vulnerabilities

title: Cloud storage breach exposes data
description: Unauthorized access to Cloud Video Storage could lead to mass exposure of recorded clips.
assumptions: Cloud provider security may be breached

title: Sensitive inferences from unfiltered data
description: Home Hub uploads raw footage without filtering sensitive contexts (e.g., private conversations, health-related activities).
assumptions: No content filtering at source

title: Inference of sensitive user habits
description: Cloud storage analyzes video content to infer user routines, preferences, or sensitive behaviors.
assumptions: Automated analysis is performed on stored data

title: User unaware of data sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that recorded clips are automatically uploaded to cloud storage.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms are unclear or buried

title: Secondary use of data beyond consent
description: Cloud Video Storage may use uploaded clips for purposes not explicitly consented to (e.g., training AI models).
assumptions: Terms of service allow broad data usage

title: Excessive motion data disclosure from Home Hub
description: The Home Hub may transmit motion alert data that exceeds what is strictly necessary for the mobile app's functionality. Motion data reveals occupancy patterns and presence information, which constitutes personal data. If the Home Hub includes unnecessary metadata (e.g., precise timestamps, sensor IDs, location details) beyond what the backend requires, this violates the minimality principle and creates avoidable data disclosure.
assumptions: Motion alerts contain personal data about household occupancy patterns; the Home Hub has discretion over what data to include in alerts

title: Motion alert data linkability in transit
description: Motion alert data transmitted over the flow could be linked with other data flows or external datasets to build profiles of household occupancy patterns. Even if individual alerts seem innocuous, the timing, frequency, and patterns of motion alerts can be correlated to identify when residents are home, away, or following specific routines.
assumptions: Motion alert data includes timing information that could be correlated across multiple alerts or with other data sources

title: Motion data exposure at Mobile App Backend
description: The Mobile App Backend receives motion alert data and may expose it to parties beyond the intended scope (e.g., third-party analytics, cloud storage providers, or through data breaches). Personal data about home occupancy patterns could be excessively exposed if the backend shares, stores, or processes this data beyond what users reasonably expect.
assumptions: The backend may share or store motion data with third parties or in ways not transparent to users

title: Motion detection data disclosure
description: The mobile app backend shares motion detection events with the homeowner, disclosing information about when and where movement occurred in the home. This reveals occupancy patterns and activity timing.
assumptions: Motion detection data is considered sensitive personal information about home occupancy

title: Notification flow linkability
description: The notification flow can be monitored to link the homeowner to specific times and locations of motion events, creating a pattern of home activity that could be correlated with other data sources.
assumptions: Network traffic or notification metadata could be intercepted or logged

title: Homeowner identifiability through notification
description: The notification flow contains or enables identification of the specific homeowner receiving motion alerts, potentially through device identifiers, account information, or notification metadata.
assumptions: Notification system includes identifying information about the recipient

title: Notification history aggregation
description: The homeowner's phone aggregates motion detection notifications over time, creating a detailed log of home activity patterns that could be accessed by malicious actors or used for profiling.
assumptions: Notification history is stored on the device and could be accessed

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of what motion detection data is being collected, how frequently notifications are sent, or what metadata accompanies each notification.
assumptions: Users may not read privacy policies or understand technical data flows

title: Users Unaware of Data Sharing
description: Users may not be informed that their aggregated device-usage analytics are shared with an external vendor, violating transparency principles.
assumptions: App privacy policy does not explicitly disclose third-party analytics sharing.

title: Vendor Non-Compliance with Regulations
description: Cloud analytics vendor may process data without adequate legal basis or compliance with data protection laws (e.g., GDPR).
assumptions: Vendor operates in jurisdiction with differing privacy standards.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure
description: Vendor could inadvertently or maliciously expose aggregated analytics data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Vendor lacks robust access controls or data security measures.

title: Inference of Sensitive Attributes
description: Vendor may infer sensitive user information (e.g., health status, location patterns) from aggregated usage analytics.
assumptions: Aggregation granularity allows re-identification or pattern analysis.
uncertainty_note: Depends on aggregation methodology; higher risk if per-user/device data is retained.

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Transit
description: Analytics data could be altered during transmission between backend and vendor if encryption or integrity checks are absent.
assumptions: Data flow lacks end-to-end encryption or tamper detection.
uncertainty_note: Assumes no transport-layer security; mitigated if HTTPS/TLS is enforced.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Mobile app backend may retain retrieved video clips longer than necessary for the homeowner's playback purpose, violating data minimization and storage limitation principles.
assumptions: Backend processes and potentially caches video data beyond immediate playback needs

title: Unauthorized disclosure during data retrieval
description: Video data in transit from cloud storage to backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if transmission is not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data transmission between DS2 and P2 may lack adequate encryption or security controls

title: Data misuse beyond intended purpose
description: Mobile app backend could process or use retrieved video clips for purposes beyond homeowner playback, such as analytics, profiling, or sharing with third parties.
assumptions: Backend has capability to process video data beyond simple retrieval and playback

title: Linkability through retrieval metadata
description: Metadata about video retrieval requests (timing, frequency, specific clips) could be used to link and profile homeowner behavior and activities.
assumptions: Retrieval requests contain identifiable metadata that could be correlated
